title: sys_member list view: a User filter (the searchable user picker), so an organization's members can be found by name from the Members tab's View all
body:
Ruled: 6289508074 · letter E′ · 2026-10-20T11:09Z

## Problem

On the organization record page (Setup → `sys_organization` → **Members** tab), an org with 1,002 members shows a 25-row related list with **no way to search**. A maintainer asked a plain question — "is this person a member of this org?" — and the only answer today is paging through 40 pages, or going the other way round (open the user's record → **Organizations** tab).

This is not specific to members: every `record:related_list` (contacts on an account, lines on an order, team members, …) has the same gap.

## Why it can't be fixed by "just turning the magnifier on"

Verified against `main` (objectstack `0904d85`, objectui `2d8a8b7`):

1. **objectui — the existing box is client-side and matches raw ids.** `RelatedList.tsx` has an opt-in `filterable` input, but `record-related-list.tsx` never passes it, so no page can show it. Even if shown, it sweeps `row[key]` — for `user_id` that is `usr_…`, not the name the cell draws — and while a term is typed it drops out of windowed mode and downloads the whole child collection.
2. **objectstack — `$search` never traverses a lookup.** `search-filter.ts` expands over the object's own textual/enum fields. `sys_member` is a junction (two lookups, formula title), so its resolved search set is empty and, since #24284, a non-blank `search` on it is refused `400 INVALID_FIELD`. A related list that forwarded the term to the server would get a 400.

## Proposal

### Part 1 — objectstack: lookup-aware `$search` (the core)

- A **single-valued lookup** in an object's search set matches when its **referenced record** matches the term on the referenced object's own resolved search fields (e.g. `sys_member.user_id` → `sys_user` name / email; pinyin via the `__search` companion where enabled).
- Expansion: run the term against the referenced object **under the caller's execution context** (RLS + FLS apply — otherwise search becomes an existence oracle for records the caller cannot read), then OR `{ <lookup>: { $in: … } }` into the term's clause. One hop only, never recursive.
- Scale: prefer a semi-join (subquery) when both objects share a datasource; cross-datasource falls back to an id list capped at N (e.g. 500) and the response says the result may be incomplete — never a silent short answer.
- Resolution: explicit `searchableFields` may name a lookup; the auto-default adds single-valued lookups whose target has a non-empty search set. `sys_member` then searches with no metadata change and the #24284 refusal no longer fires for it.
- Record the rule as an addendum to ADR-0061.
- Free side-benefit: main list views ("search accounts by owner name"), lookup pickers, REST and MCP/AI reads get the same behaviour.

### Part 2 — spec: `record:related_list.searchable`

- New `searchable?: boolean` on `RecordRelatedListProps`, default `true`; `false` hides the box. Enforced in the renderer per ADR-0049 (pin test), not declared-only.

### Part 3 — objectui: the search box on the related list

Where the user types — **in the related-list card header**, the same magnifier control the main list toolbar uses:

```
default
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 👥 Members  1002                  🔍   [Invite user] [Add member] │

after clicking 🔍 — expands in place inside the header
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 👥 Members  1 / 1002   [🔍 Zhang Yang        ×]  [Invite user] [Add member] │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Zhang Yang    Member     2026/10/15 4:30 PM          ···    │
│                          View all results for "Zhang Yang" → │

no match
│        No members match "Zhang San"     [Invite user]      │
```

| Aspect | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Placeholder | derived from the searchable columns, e.g. "Search user, role…" |
| Trigger | 300 ms debounce; Enter searches immediately |
| Count badge | "matched / total" while a term is active |
| Paging | stays windowed — term sent as `$search`, server pages; never a full download |
| Clear | × or Esc clears and collapses |
| Tabs | each related list keeps its own term |
| View all | link carries the term (`?search=…`); the list page already reads an initial term |
| Mobile | expands to a full-width row under the header |
| Hidden when | the object resolves no search field (reuse ListView's "searchless object" handling on `INVALID_FIELD`) or `searchable: false` |

- Retire the client-side `filterable` prop (inert today, and wrong if switched on) under enforce-or-remove, after confirming it has no consumers.
- i18n for placeholder / no-match / incomplete-result strings (en, zh, ja, es).

## Acceptance

1. Org page → Members → 🔍 → type a member's name: only that member is listed, badge shows `1 / 1002`, the request is a windowed `$search` (no full-collection fetch).
2. A non-member's name: "No members match …" with the card's existing Invite action.
3. With pinyin search enabled, `zy` finds 张杨.
4. A user the caller cannot read is not found by name (RLS/FLS honoured in the lookup hop).
5. Invitations tab searches by email, Teams tab by name.
6. "View all" opens the full list with the same term applied.
7. A business object's related list (e.g. Account → Contacts) is searchable with no metadata change.

## Delivery

1. objectstack PR — lookup-aware `$search` + ADR-0061 addendum + tests (permissions, cap, pinyin) + spec `searchable`.
2. objectui PR — header search box, `filterable` retirement, renderer wiring, i18n, browser-verified on the org Members tab.

Workaround until then: open the user's record → **Organizations** tab.
